title: Reject bool JSON path indices instead of rendering invalid array paths
problem: JSONIndexType._format_value and JSONPathType._format_value test array indices with isinstance(value, int). bool is an int subclass, so json_col[True] renders the path $[True] and ("items", False) renders $."items"[False], which are not JSON array indices. Decide a bool contract (reject with an actionable error), apply it to the single and the nested path formatter for both bind and literal rendering, keep int (0, 1, negative) and string-key output byte for byte, and document the supported path component types.
non_goals: no change to other JSON operators, string-key escaping or integer index output
no claim that a live CUBRID server was exercised unless a live run is recorded

live: python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -m integration test/test_integration.py -k json

expected: A bool path component raises TypeError: execution reports it as sqlalchemy.exc.StatementError before any SQL is sent (bound), and literal_binds rendering as sqlalchemy.exc.CompileError (compiled). Integer and string components render exactly as before.
